mcqs.question: A person pushes a wall with a force of 50 N but the wall does not move. Which statement correctly describes the work done by the person?

options.A: Positive work is done because a force is applied.
options.B: No work is done because there is no displacement.
options.C: Negative work is done because the wall resists the force.
options.D: Work is done only if the wall moves in the direction opposite to the force.

mcqs.answer: No work is done because there is no displacement.
mcqs.explanation: Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force. If displacement is zero, the product is zero, so no work is done. Option B states this correctly. Options A, C and D incorrectly assume work depends only on the presence of force or on direction without considering displacement.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: Which of the following situations results in the greatest amount of work done by the applied force?

options.A: A 10 N horizontal force moves an object 5 m upward.
options.B: A 10 N vertical upward force moves an object 5 m upward.
options.C: A 10 N horizontal force moves an object 5 m opposite to the direction of the force.
options.D: A 10 N vertical upward force moves an object 5 m downward.

mcqs.answer: A 10 N vertical upward force moves an object 5 m upward.
mcqs.explanation: Work is maximum when the force and displacement are in the same direction, giving W = F × s. In option B, the force and displacement are both upward, so W = 10 N × 5 m = 50 J. In A the force is horizontal while displacement is vertical, giving zero work (force perpendicular to displacement). In C the force opposes displacement, giving negative work. In D the force opposes displacement, also giving negative work. Hence B yields the greatest positive work.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question:
Two tasks are performed:
1. Lifting a 2 kg box vertically through a height of 3 m.
2. Pulling a sled with a constant horizontal force of 20 N over a distance of 2 m.
Which statement correctly compares the work done in the two tasks?

options.A: The work done in task 1 (≈60 J) is greater than the work done in task 2 (40 J).
options.B: The work done in task 2 (40 J) is greater than the work done in task 1 (≈60 J).
options.C: Both tasks involve the same amount of work, 50 J each.
options.D: No work is done in either task because the forces are not applied in the direction of motion.

mcqs.answer: The work done in task 1 (≈60 J) is greater than the work done in task 2 (40 J).
mcqs.explanation: Work for lifting: W = m g h = 2 kg × 10 m/s² × 3 m = 60 J. Work for pulling: W = F × s = 20 N × 2 m = 40 J. Therefore task 1 involves more work. Option A states this correctly. Options B and C give incorrect comparisons, and D is wrong because the forces are aligned with the displacements, so work is indeed done.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to one joule (1 J) in SI base units?
mcqs.explanation: A joule is defined as the work done when a force of one newton acts through a displacement of one metre, i.e., 1 J = 1 N × 1 m = 1 N·m. Option A matches this definition. Option B (kg·m/s) is a unit of momentum, not energy. Option C (N·s) is the unit of impulse. Option D (V·A·s) equals a coulomb, not a joule.

mcqs.question: In physics, work is defined as:

options.A: The product of force and the distance moved in the direction of the force.
options.B: The energy stored in a stretched spring.
options.C: The rate at which a force is applied.
options.D: The product of mass and acceleration.

mcqs.answer: The product of force and the distance moved in the direction of the force.
mcqs.explanation: Work (W) = F × s × cosθ, which reduces to the product of force and displacement when the force is along the direction of motion. Option A captures this definition. Option B describes elastic potential energy, C describes power, and D describes force (Newton's second law).

mcqs.question: A person pulls a cart with a rope. Which statement correctly identifies the force and the displacement in this situation?

options.A: Force is the tension in the rope; displacement is the distance the cart moves.
options.B: Force is the weight of the cart; displacement is the length of the rope.
options.C: Force is the friction between wheels and ground; displacement is the height the cart is lifted.
options.D: Force is the normal reaction from the ground; displacement is the time taken to pull the cart.

mcqs.answer: Force is the tension in the rope; displacement is the distance the cart moves.
mcqs.explanation: When pulling, the applied force is the tension transmitted through the rope, and the cart’s displacement is the linear distance it travels. Option A states this correctly. The other options misidentify either the force or the displacement.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes when work is done on an object?

options.A: Work is done only when a force causes a displacement, even if the force is perpendicular to the displacement.
options.B: Work is done when there is a force and any displacement, regardless of direction.
options.C: Work is done only when the component of the force along the displacement is non‑zero.
options.D: Work is done whenever energy is transferred, irrespective of the presence of a force.

mcqs.answer: Work is done only when the component of the force along the displacement is non‑zero.
mcqs.explanation: Work depends on the dot product of force and displacement: W = F · s = F s cosθ. If the component of force along the displacement (cosθ ≠ 0) is zero, no work is done. Option C captures this condition. Option A is wrong because a perpendicular force (θ = 90°) does no work. Option B ignores direction, and D confuses work with general energy transfer.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question: A constant horizontal force of 15 N pulls a crate through a distance of 4 m. What is the work done on the crate?
mcqs.explanation: Work = force × displacement = 15 N × 4 m = 60 J. Option C gives the correct value. The other options result from incorrect multiplication.
